answer: An agent economy can make identity expensive by requiring every new agent to lock a bond before it may trade, vote, or relay evidence. Existing agents issue signed challenge tasks during a voyage, and conflicting answers or collusion proofs slash the bond and lower reputation. Honest agents on each ridge and reef can therefore quarantine newcomers until they earn history. A Sybil attacker must fund many bonds and sustain costly, consistent behavior, while one detected fake burns its capital.
